about: Provenance of the data published by ShakeReady: sources, processing, recorded decisions, checks and file checksums.
code_version_note: The repository commit in place when this file was generated. The commit that publishes this file is the next one.
prepared_by: ShakeReady's code, namely the bridge inventory builder, the HAZUS bridge fragilities and the damage calculation, was made by E. Taciroglu, as was SR-HazardMaker. The processing, transcription and checks described here were carried out in November 2026 with an AI assistant (Claude, made by Anthropic) working at his direction. Values taken from published documents were transcribed and then compared against those documents by script.

nbi-2025-ca.title: National Bridge Inventory, 2025, California, comma-delimited file (CA25.txt)
nbi-2025-ca.publisher: Federal Highway Administration, U.S. Department of Transportation
nbi-2025-ca.note: FHWA's download page gives 25,975 highway bridges for California in 2025 and states that 2025 was the last year submitted in the Coding Guide format. A copy of the file is kept in the project's archive.

hazus-6.1.title: Hazus Earthquake Model Technical Manual, Hazus 6.1, July 2024
hazus-6.1.note: Section 7.1, Highway Transportation System: Tables 7-1, 7-2 and 7-6, Equations 7-1 to 7-4, and the worked example in Section 7.1.6.2. The manual credits Basoz and Mander (1999) for the theory behind the bridge damage functions.

datasets.title: NBI bridges, California, 2025
processing: Read the comma-delimited file (single quote as text qualifier). All 25,975 records are of record type 1, the route carried on the structure, and all are kept.
Convert latitude (Item 16) and longitude (Item 17) from packed degrees, minutes and seconds to decimal degrees; west longitude is made negative.
Decode material and design codes (Item 43 for the main spans, Item 44 for approach spans) and county codes (Item 3) to names.
Carry over year built and reconstructed, lanes, traffic, span counts and lengths, skew and condition ratings as recorded.
Assign each record its HAZUS highway bridge class (see the fragility set).

datasets.title: HAZUS highway bridges (fragility set)
processing: Transcribe the classification scheme (Table 7-1), the K3D coefficients (Table 7-2) and the median values (Table 7-6).
Implement Equations 7-1 to 7-4 and the damage algorithm for ground shaking.
Record every choice made where the manual is silent or inconsistent (decisions HZ-01 to HZ-11).

fragility_decisions.choice: A California bridge built in 1975 or later is classed as seismic design; elsewhere the year is 1990.
fragility_decisions.basis: Table 7-1 gives the year in every row. The sentence introducing the table states the two years the other way round (1990 in California, 1975 elsewhere). The table is followed because it is explicit row by row and agrees with earlier editions of the Hazus documentation.
fragility_decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.
fragility_decisions.effect: 3,726 bridges built from 1975 to 1989 are classed as seismic design; under the other reading they would be conventional.

fragility_decisions.topic: Form of the span factor K3D
fragility_decisions.choice: K3D = 1 + A / (N - B), with A and B from Table 7-2 and N the number of spans.
fragility_decisions.basis: Table 7-2 and the accompanying text give this form. Equation 7-3 is printed as (1 + A) / (N - B), but the manual's worked example evaluates it to 1.125 for A = 0.25, B = 1 and N = 3, which only the Table 7-2 form gives.
fragility_decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.
fragility_decisions.effect: Applies to the 14,717 bridges with more than one span and a K3D equation.

fragility_decisions.choice: K3D is taken as 1 when N - B is zero or negative.
fragility_decisions.basis: The formula is undefined in that case and the manual does not say what to do. A factor of 1 leaves the class medians unchanged.
fragility_decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

fragility_decisions.choice: K3D is taken as 1 and the spectral-shape factor is not applied. The skew factor still applies.
fragility_decisions.basis: Table 7-1 gives no K3D equation and no I-shape value for HWB28.
fragility_decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

fragility_decisions.choice: N is NBI Item 45, the number of spans in the main unit. Approach spans (Item 46) are not counted.
fragility_decisions.basis: The manual's worked example takes the number of spans from Item 45.
fragility_decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.
fragility_decisions.effect: 1,232 bridges have approach spans that are not counted.

fragility_decisions.choice: 'Length less than 20 m' is evaluated on NBI Item 49, the structure length.
fragility_decisions.basis: Table 7-1 does not name the NBI item. Step 1 of the damage algorithm lists bridge length separately from maximum span length, so the total length is used.
fragility_decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.
fragility_decisions.effect: Decides the class of 1,112 steel bridges, of which 165 are under 20 m.

fragility_decisions.choice: A skew coded 99 is evaluated as 45 degrees. Any other value of 90 or more is evaluated as 0.
fragility_decisions.basis: The NBI uses 99 when skew varies along the bridge, and the manual does not address this code. 45 degrees is unfavorable but bounded. A published implementation for Texas bridges treats the same code with its 45-degree adjustment (Khosravikia et al., 2020, CTR Technical Report 5-6916-01-1).
fragility_decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

fragility_decisions.choice: Only damage from ground shaking is evaluated.
fragility_decisions.basis: The manual's ground-failure functions need permanent ground deformation at each site, and no such hazard layer is available here.
fragility_decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

fragility_decisions.choice: Culverts are kept in the inventory and classified by the same rules as bridges.
fragility_decisions.basis: The NBI records culverts as structures and Table 7-1 has no separate rule for them. Bridge curves fit culverts poorly, and users may wish to exclude them.
fragility_decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.
fragility_decisions.effect: 3,571 culverts: 203 in HWB3, 131 in HWB4, 3,237 in HWB28.

fragility_decisions.choice: The design era is taken from the year built alone.
fragility_decisions.basis: The NBI has no field for seismic retrofit. The year of reconstruction is not used, because a reconstruction is not necessarily a seismic one. Bridges retrofitted after construction are therefore treated as unretrofitted.
fragility_decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.
fragility_decisions.effect: 14,039 bridges are classed as conventional design; 3,756 of them have a reconstruction year on record.

fragility_decisions.topic: Slight-damage median shown on the map
fragility_decisions.choice: Bridge popups show the class value for slight damage, without the spectral-shape factor.
fragility_decisions.basis: The factor needs Sa(0.3 s) and Sa(1.0 s) at the site, which come from a hazard layer. It is applied when damage is computed.
fragility_decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.
fragility_decisions.effect: 14,198 bridges are in classes where the factor can apply.

inventory_decisions.choice: All records in the FHWA highway-bridge file are included.
inventory_decisions.basis: The file holds only record type 1 (the route carried on the structure), so no record is a duplicate view of another.

inventory_decisions.choice: A record is placed on the map only if its coordinates fall inside a bounding box around California (32.0 to 42.1 north, 124.6 to 114.0 west). Other records are listed in the CSV without coordinates.
inventory_decisions.basis: Guards against missing or mistyped coordinates in the source.

inventory_decisions.choice: When a bridge has no approach spans (Item 46 is zero), its approach material and design are shown as None.
inventory_decisions.basis: The source codes these as 'other', which reads as if a material were present.

inventory_decisions.choice: A value of zero in Item 106 means the bridge has not been reconstructed.

inventory_decisions.topic: Names of what a bridge carries and crosses
inventory_decisions.choice: Item 7 (facility carried) and Item 6A (feature intersected) are shown as recorded, with repeated spaces removed.
inventory_decisions.basis: No spelling or capitalization is changed, so the text can be matched to the source.

inventory_decisions.choice: Every attribute in the original files is carried over unchanged.
inventory_decisions.basis: The building layers are an archive of the original team's work, not a new compilation.

inventory_decisions.topic: Positions of the six non-ductile buildings
inventory_decisions.choice: Their positions are taken from the Latitude and Longitude attributes in the file (for example '34.0488 N' and '118.2595 W'), with west made negative.
inventory_decisions.basis: The original file stored only street addresses for these six, which the original map service located on the fly.

inventory_decisions.choice: The bridge data from the original site (about 2016, 25,431 records) is archived and no longer shown.
inventory_decisions.basis: Replaced by the 2025 file. The earlier snapshot lacked span counts and condition ratings, and 60 of its records had no coordinates.

damage_decisions.choice: The value at an asset is found by bilinear interpolation between the four grid nodes around it.
damage_decisions.basis: Hazard layers are grids; assets lie between nodes. Bilinear interpolation is the simplest method that varies smoothly and adds no information of its own.

damage_decisions.choice: A node without a value is left out and the remaining nodes' weights are rescaled. An asset outside the grid, or with no valid node around it, gets no estimate and is listed with blank cells.
damage_decisions.basis: Avoids inventing ground motion where the layer has none, such as offshore or beyond the edge of a scenario.

damage_decisions.choice: A layer's values are used as published. No further adjustment is made for the soil at each asset.
damage_decisions.basis: Each layer states the ground condition its values assume. If that is a uniform reference condition, shaking on softer ground is understated, and so is damage there.

damage_decisions.choice: The probability of reaching a more severe state is not allowed to exceed that of a milder one.
damage_decisions.basis: After the manual's adjustments, the median for a more severe state can fall at or below that of a milder one (for example where a class has equal medians for two states). Without this rule a state could receive a negative probability.

damage_decisions.topic: Results from a probabilistic hazard map
damage_decisions.choice: Each asset is evaluated at its own site's ground motion for the chosen probability level.
damage_decisions.basis: A hazard map does not describe one earthquake: its values would not all occur together. Results are therefore per asset. Totals across assets are shown as a description of the inventory, not as the loss from an event.

damage_decisions.topic: Expected number in each damage state
damage_decisions.choice: The expected number of assets in a state is the sum of their probabilities of being in that state.
damage_decisions.basis: Standard for expected counts. It carries the caution in DMG-05 when the layer is probabilistic.

damage_decisions.topic: A single label for a bridge
damage_decisions.choice: Two labels are computed. The dashboard colors by the worst damage state a bridge has at least a 50% chance of reaching or exceeding. The table also gives the single most likely of the five states, with a tie going to the milder one.
damage_decisions.basis: The single most likely state can mislead: 'None' is often the largest of five probabilities even where damage has a sizable chance, because that chance is split among four damage states. In a magnitude 7 test scenario on rock, all 135 bridges within 2 km of the fault were labeled None by that rule, though 35 of them had a 25 to 58 percent chance of some damage. The 50% rule is easier to read correctly, and the popup leads with the chance of any damage. The five probabilities are always given.

damage_decisions.choice: Values are given to four decimal places, an exact half rounded up. Coordinates are given to five.
damage_decisions.basis: Stated so that the table can be reproduced exactly by the reference code.

damage_decisions.choice: The dashboard can color each bridge by its probability of reaching or exceeding a chosen damage state: slight, moderate, extensive or complete. Probabilities are shown in seven classes with breaks at 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 and 75 percent. A numbered circle standing for several bridges shows their average.
damage_decisions.basis: The probability of reaching or exceeding a state is what a fragility curve gives directly, and it is the quantity most decisions are framed in. The classes are finer at the low end because the probability of the more severe states is often small. The average over a group of bridges is the expected fraction of them reaching that state.

hazard_decisions.choice: Ground motions are stored in thousandths of g. An exact half rounds up.
hazard_decisions.basis: 0.001 g is finer than any of the sources warrant, and whole numbers keep the files small. The rounding rule is stated so that the two converters, in the browser and on the command line, give identical files.

hazard_decisions.topic: Area kept from the USGS hazard model
hazard_decisions.choice: USGS hazard-model tables are cropped to latitude 32.0 to 42.5 north and longitude 125.0 to 113.5 west.
hazard_decisions.basis: The national files cover the conterminous United States. The crop keeps California with a margin, so that every structure has grid nodes on all sides.

hazard_decisions.choice: Each measure is converted to g from the units the file states for it. Percent of g is recognized in both spellings found in USGS files, 'pctg' and '%g'. A file with any other unit is refused.
hazard_decisions.basis: USGS changed the spelling between software versions. Reading the unit from the file avoids assuming it.

hazard_decisions.choice: The whole grid is kept. The spacing is taken as the grid's extent divided by its number of intervals, and each row is placed by its own coordinates.
hazard_decisions.basis: The file's stated spacing is rounded to four decimals, which would drift across several hundred nodes. Placing rows by their coordinates does not depend on the order in which the file lists them.

hazard_decisions.choice: A ShakeMap layer is labeled site-specific.
hazard_decisions.basis: ShakeMap estimates the shaking at the ground surface using its own map of ground conditions, so no uniform reference condition applies.

hazard_decisions.choice: The points must form an evenly spaced grid in latitude and longitude. Accelerations in cm/s² or m/s² are converted with g = 9.80665 m/s².
hazard_decisions.basis: Scattered points would need a gridding method, which is a modeling choice that belongs to whoever produced the ground motions.

hazard_decisions.choice: SR-HazardMaker will not build a layer without a title, a ground condition, a source title, a publisher or author, and a date. It fills these in only when the file itself identifies them.
hazard_decisions.basis: A layer whose origin is unknown cannot support a traceable result.

hazard_decisions.choice: A layer made with SR-HazardMaker, or opened from a file on the user's computer, can be used on the dashboard without being published. It is marked as the user's own, and any damage table made from it states that it is not part of the ShakeReady repository and gives its checksum.
hazard_decisions.basis: Lets people work with their own ground motions at once, without letting an unreviewed layer pass for a published one.

hazard_decisions.choice: SR-HazardMaker is kept in its own repository. This site copies a tagged release of it without changes and records the release, the commit and a checksum of each copied file.
hazard_decisions.basis: A single source for the converters, in the browser and on the command line, so that the public tool and the one this site uses cannot drift apart.

scenario_decisions.choice: Scenarios are computed with the model of Boore, Stewart, Seyhan and Atkinson (2014), Earthquake Spectra 30(3), 1057-1085: its base model, for the RotD50 horizontal component.
scenario_decisions.basis: A widely used model for shallow crustal earthquakes in California that needs only magnitude, style of faulting, distance to the fault and Vs30. It is the first model offered; others can be added beside it.

scenario_decisions.topic: Where the model's numbers come from
scenario_decisions.choice: The equations were written from the paper. The coefficient values were taken from the table in the OpenQuake engine's implementation of the model.
scenario_decisions.basis: No number enters the tool from memory. The code is then held to that engine's verification tables (see the checks).

scenario_decisions.choice: No regional adjustment to attenuation and no basin-depth term are applied.
scenario_decisions.basis: The base model is the authors' recommendation for California. The basin term needs the depth to a velocity horizon at each site, which a single-Vs30 scenario does not have.

scenario_decisions.choice: One Vs30 is used everywhere in a scenario. The default is 760 m/s.
scenario_decisions.basis: Keeps the scenario fully described by a handful of inputs. Shaking on softer ground than the chosen Vs30 is understated; the layer says which Vs30 was used.

scenario_decisions.choice: The rupture is a flat rectangle: a straight trace between two points, a dip, and a down-dip width. A dipping fault dips to the right of the direction from the first point to the second. The trace's length is whatever the two points give; it is not adjusted to the magnitude.
scenario_decisions.basis: The model needs only the distance to the rupture's surface projection. Leaving the length to the user avoids building in a magnitude-length relation; the user is responsible for a length that suits the magnitude.

scenario_decisions.choice: Distances are measured in a flat local frame centered on the fault, with a spherical Earth of radius 6,371 km.
scenario_decisions.basis: Accurate to well under one percent over the few hundred kilometers a scenario covers, and simple enough to be identical in the browser and on the command line.

scenario_decisions.topic: Shaking levels other than the median
scenario_decisions.choice: A scenario can be the median or the median shifted by a chosen number of standard deviations, applied equally at every point. The nonlinear site term always uses the median shaking on rock, as the model specifies.
scenario_decisions.basis: A uniform shift is a simple way to look at a stronger or weaker outcome. It is not a simulated realization of the event, which would vary from place to place, and the layer says so.

scenario_decisions.choice: The tool refuses magnitudes outside 3 to 8.5 (3 to 7 for normal faulting) and Vs30 outside 150 to 1500 m/s, and does not let the grid extend more than 250 km beyond the fault.
scenario_decisions.basis: These are the ranges the authors give for the model.

scenario_decisions.choice: A scenario cannot be built without naming who made it, and every input is written into the layer.
scenario_decisions.basis: A computed scenario has no outside source to point to, so its maker and its inputs are its provenance. With them, anyone can recompute it.

verification.result: 25,975 records read, equal to the count FHWA publishes for California in 2025.
For the 24,415 bridges present in both the 2025 file and the earlier snapshot, 95% of locations agree to within about 6 meters and 99% have the same year built.
The longest span in the file is the Golden Gate Bridge at 1,280.2 m, the correct value.
A script compared the transcribed values with the text of the manual: all 28 sets of medians match, as do the K3D equation, I-shape value and design era of the 27 classes that have them.
The classification function returns the class given in every row of Table 7-1.
Reproduced: class HWB17, K3D = 1.125, and damage-state probabilities 0.183, 0.205, 0.165, 0.255, 0.192 against the manual's rounded 0.18, 0.20, 0.16, 0.26, 0.20.

verification.check: The dashboard against the reference code
verification.result: For 425 sampled bridges, covering every class present, the adjusted medians computed in the browser equal those of the reference code to rounding error.
Each filter tested returns the same number of bridges as an independent count from the data file.

verification.check: Damage calculation against an independent implementation
verification.result: The table produced by the dashboard was compared with the one produced by separate reference code (tools/damage_reference.py), using made-up test layers that are not published: a hazard map at two probability levels and a scenario. For all 25,974 bridges the two tables are identical, character for character.
The expected counts shown on the dashboard equal the sums from the reference table. A table downloaded with a county filter applied contains exactly the reference rows for that county.

Seven real USGS ShakeMap grid files (shortened samples from the OpenQuake engine's test data, three versions of the ShakeMap software, both unit spellings): every row read lands on the right grid node with the right value. For a full grid in the same layout, all 81,993 values match the source after conversion from percent of g, zipped or not.
A table in cm/s² with its own column names and rows in random order is placed correctly on its grid and converted to g.

verification.check: An SR-HazardMaker layer on the dashboard
verification.result: A layer made in SR-HazardMaker and opened on the dashboard gives a damage table identical, for all 25,974 bridges, to the reference code run on the same layer file. The checksum shown equals the file's.

verification.check: SR-HazardMaker: browser and command line against each other
verification.result: The tool's own test suite (21 tests, run automatically on every change) builds the same inputs with the Python converters and with the browser converters and requires the same layer from both: USGS-style tables given separately, in an archive and in a ZIP64 archive; ShakeMap grids with either unit spelling, any field order and any row order, zipped or not; and a plain table in cm/s². Reading a value at a point must agree exactly at 4,000 random points. On this site, a 290 MB archive gave the same layer, with only the three tables needed read from it.

verification.check: A layer file opened on the dashboard
verification.result: A layer file opened from the computer on the dashboard gives the same damage table as the reference code for all 25,974 bridges. A file that is not a layer is refused.

verification.check: The ground-motion model against reference values
verification.result: The model as implemented was compared with all 600 cases of the verification tables distributed with the OpenQuake engine for Boore et al. (2014): magnitudes 3 to 8, three styles of faulting and unspecified, distances to 100 km, Vs30 from 200 to 760 m/s, for PGA and spectral acceleration at 0.3 s and 1.0 s. The 1,800 medians agree to within 5 parts per million and the 1,800 standard deviations to within 0.00005, the precision of the tables. A subset of 69 cases is checked automatically on every change to the tool.

Distances to a vertical and to a dipping fault match hand-computed values. A scenario built on the page and the same scenario built on the command line are the same layer, value for value (43,248 values in the case tested), and three further scenarios agree in the tool's own tests. A scenario layer opened on the dashboard gives a damage table identical to the reference code.

limits: The HAZUS curves describe classes of bridges, not individual structures. They suit screening an inventory, not conclusions about one bridge.
The NBI does not record seismic retrofits, so retrofitted bridges are treated as built (decision HZ-10).
Culverts are in the inventory and are given bridge curves, which fit them poorly (decision HZ-09).
Only ground shaking is considered. Liquefaction, landslide and fault-rupture displacement are not (decision HZ-08).
NBI values are as submitted by the owning agencies. No value has been corrected.
The building layers date from 2017 and have not been updated.
